title: Install readiness: spot-check validation suite for Private VPC installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Private (VPC) installs frequently fail late in customer setups due to quota limits, IAM permissions, DNS delegation, or insufficient GPU capacity in target regions. This ticket scopes a lightweight, automated "spot-check" validation suite that runs before/after Terraform apply to surface deterministic, actionable failures and remediation guidance. Goals: 1) Provide an executable pre-install checklist that can be run locally, in CI, or remotely via ops. 2) Cover critical failure modes: cloud quotas (vCPUs, GPUs, ENIs), IAM/service account permissions, DNS zone/record delegation, default VPC conflicts, and GPU SKUs availability for requested instance types. 3) Emit machine-readable diagnostics (JSON) plus human-friendly remediation steps and links to suggested Terraform module toggles. 4) Integrate with our onboarding flow (console + docs) so customers and SEs can run the same checks we run in-house.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A CLI tool (check-vpc-install) that performs at least: quota checks, IAM permission simulation, DNS delegation verification, and GPU SKU availability check against a target region and outputs a JSON report. 2) Terraform plan hook sample that demonstrates calling the CLI in a pre-commit or pre-apply job. 3) Runbook entry in Confluence with example remediation snippets for common failures. 4) Automated GitHub Actions workflow template that returns non-zero on blocking failures and annotates PRs with the diagnosis. 5) Unit tests that mock cloud APIs for the most common failure modes.
implementation_notes: Proposed approach: - Build a thin orchestration binary in Go (single static binary) that can be embedded in Terraform pipelines and run in our CI images. - Use provider SDK calls (AWS/GCP/Azure) rather than raw IAM policy eval where available (call service-quotas, iam simulate-principal-policy, compute/gce quotas, and NLB/ENI limits). - GPU capacity check: query instance-type availability using DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings/AZ capacity checks and our internal capacity signals (if available). Provide clear fallback: recommend alternative SKUs or region suggestions. - DNS: validate that provided zone ID matches delegation records and that example A/CNAME records resolve to expected targets; detect conflicting public/private zone names. - Output: {summary, severity, checks: [...] } as compact JSON and a verbose markdown diagnostic for PR comments. - Terraform examples: use local-exec null_resource in examples/private-install to call the tool as a pre-apply gate and produce artifacts under terraform/.ci/prechecks.json. - Security: tool must not persist credentials; rely on environment credentials with explicit scope; avoid writing secrets into logs. - Packaging: publish binary to our artifacts S3 and include a brew-style installer for SEs.

comments: 2026-02-11 — Aisha Patel: Draft spec uploaded to Confluence. Focusing first on AWS and GCP; Azure to follow. Key variables: target-region, required-gpu-skus, expected-vpc-cidr.

2026-02-18 — Marco Li: Completed PoC for AWS quotas and IAM simulate. Found that many customer accounts block iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy — need fallback to policy introspection based on role ARN and known managed policies.

2026-02-25 — SRE Rotation (Elena Gomez): Verified GPU SKU check against our spot capacity signals; adding a warning (soft-failure) for SKU availability if capacity signals are low but not entirely blocked.
2026-03-03 — Design review (Trevor Kim): Requested clearer remediation snippets and shorter error codes to map into Console UX. Will add structured "remediation_code" in next iteration.
2026-03-09 — Marco Li: Implemented JSON report output and GitHub Actions template. PR #98 contains initial CLI and example workflow. Requesting review from Security for credential handling pattern.

2026-03-12 — Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed. Approved with note: ensure we do not call STS:GetFederationToken or any API that writes cross-account audit logs. Add explicit logging sanitization to strip account IDs in debug outputs.
risks: Cloud provider rate limits could make end-to-end checks slow or flaky — include exponential backoff and cached results for repeated runs.
iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy not available in some orgs — need safe fallbacks and explicit permission error messaging.
GPU capacity signals are probabilistic — avoid hard-blocking installs based solely on availability check; surface a confidence score instead.
DNS delegation checks may be complex when customers use split-horizon DNS — provide explicit guidance for private vs public zones.
next_steps: Merge PoC PR and enable feature-flagged GitHub Actions in example repo
Add GCP quota IAM adapters and run end-to-end checks against a staging account
Create a CLI binary release and publish to artifacts bucket
Wire diagnostics into Console onboarding page to recommend region/SKU choices
